note: Patterns that map the compiler's first error to a class of the model's CheckError, tried in order. A failed instantiation's first error carries the note of the constraint that failed. 'has no attribute 'copy'' comes before unknownAttribute: the compiler reports .copy() of a value that is not Copyable as a missing attribute, the model as notCopyable. 'has no attribute' is the compiler's error for an unknown field and for an unknown method alike, on any type. 'does not designate a value with an origin', the compiler's error for moving an element out of a list or an array, or a value out through a 'ref' binding, comes before escapingReference, whose pattern also matches 'origin'. 'use of invalidated interior reference' is the compiler's error for a reference to a list element used after the list changed. 'is uninitialized at (the implicit )?return from this function', the compiler's error for a 'mut' parameter or the 'self' of '__init__' left partly uninitialized when the function returns, comes before uninitializedUse, whose pattern also matches 'uninitialized'. 'invalid use of mutating method on rvalue' is the compiler's error for a 'mut self' method called on a value that cannot be changed, such as 'p^' or a 'read' parameter, and 'value passed to mutable argument ... must be mutable' its error for such a value passed to a 'mut' parameter; the model reports both as immutablePlace. 'has non-'Deinitable' type' is the compiler's error for a struct on a cycle of structs made only of list and array edges, and 'attempt to resolve a recursive reference to declaration' its error for a struct that holds itself by value, directly or through other structs, or through arrays alone when the structs have a __deinit__. Which of these cycles the model accepts, and the compiler bugs among them (D-0004, D-0006), is in docs/decisions/conformance-classes.md, Cycles of structs. 'does not conform to trait 'Writable'' is the compiler's error for printing a value that print cannot write. 'aliasing values passed immutably' is the compiler's error for a location passed immutably that a 'mut' argument of the same call aliases, such as a returned reference and the place it points into; 'immutable' does not match 'immutably'. 'value passed to mutable argument ... must be mutable' is also the compiler's error for a 'mut' argument that is a call returning an immutable reference, and for a temporary passed 'mut', which the model reports as notAPlace (#81). 'no matching function in initialization' is the compiler's error for every initialization whose arguments fit no initializer: a construction with wrong arguments, a literal that does not fit the list or array it initializes, and List[T](...) with arguments or from a source that is not a list or an array of T, or range(...) of Int arguments with T an Int. 'cannot construct 'T' with itself, you can remove the constructor call' is its error for the same misfit when the one argument has the type T itself, such as List[T](xs) from a List[T] whose elements cannot be copied (#103). 'function instantiation failed: constraint failed: expected N elements in the SIMD list literal, found M', the failed instantiation with its note, is its error for a literal of any length but 1 where an Int, SIMD[DType.int, 1], is expected (D-0005). 'no matching function in call to 'NAME'' is its error for a call of a function with several overloads, none of which its arguments fit, a wrong number of them included: List[T](range(...)) whose arguments fit no form of range (#121), and len of a Bool, None or a struct without Sized (#190). All four are matched whole, so that no other message reaches noMatchingInit, and the second and the fourth come first, since each holds a name that a later pattern, such as 'immutable', could match. 'used with all fields manually initialized but without calling an '__init__' method' is the compiler's error for a struct built field by field and then used whole, which the model reports as uninitializedUse, as the compiler does for a part of one (#51). 'no matching method in call to 'NAME'' is the compiler's error for a call of a method or an operator with several overloads, none of which its arguments fit, a wrong number of them included: an operator of an integer literal, an index of a list or an array, and a list's pop (#88, #169). ''T' does not implement the '__X__' method' is its error for an operator whose operand's type lacks the operator's method, and for a call of a variable, whose type lacks __call__ (#176). Both are matched whole, and come first, since each holds a name of the program's, of a type or a method, that a later pattern, such as 'immutable' or 'origin', could match. 'cannot synthesize copy constructor because field 'F' has non-copyable type 'T'' and 'cannot synthesize implicit copy constructor because field 'F' has non-implicitly-copyable type 'T'' are the compiler's errors for a struct that declares Copyable, or ImplicitlyCopyable, with a field that cannot be copied so; both are uncopyableField (#164), matched whole and first for the same reason. 'invalid call to 'F': missing required argument: 'A'' and 'invalid call to 'F': unexpected argument' are the compiler's errors for a call of a function or a method, __call__ included, that leaves out one or more required arguments, of which it names only the first, or that passes more positional arguments than it takes. Both are arityMismatch (#209, #219), matched whole and first, since the names of the callee and the argument, such as 'copy' or 'immutable', could match a later pattern. ''T' is not subscriptable, it does not implement the `__getitem__`/`__setitem__` methods' is the compiler's error for a subscript, read or assigned, of a Bool, of None or of a struct that declares neither method; it is notAList (#182), matched whole and first, since the type's name could match a later pattern. 'invalid call to 'NAME': violated constraint' is the compiler's error for a call whose constraint on the parameters of the callee's type fails, such as two arrays compared whose element type does not conform to Equatable, or to Comparable to order them; it is violatedConstraint (#166), matched whole and first, since the name could match a later pattern. 'cannot use a dynamic value in type specification' and 'cannot use a dynamic value in a parameter list' are the compiler's errors for a type, or a type inside List[...] or Array[...], whose name a variable or a parameter in scope hides; both are valueAsType (#193), matched whole.
